text:
Maria Chen: taking over evening oncall now (primary) — I'm on until 02:00 UTC. Samir will be secondary for the first hour then Priya takes over 22:00 UTC. leaving notes below for anyone joining the bridge :point_down:

Maria Chen: current state — no open P0s, aber-search has degraded 15% QPS success rate in EU, but falling within SLO for now. customers hitting timeouts on long sequences.

Ops Bot: Incident monitor: aber-search error rate elevated (15% -> 28% in last 10m) — alert threshold breached :rotating_light:. Alert link: https://monitoring.redwood/alerts/INC-4321

Samir Patel: thanks. i'm on the bridge. quick checks: k8s pods for search-pool?

Maria Chen: logs show repeated OOMKill on gpu-inference-2. suspect batching spike. runbook: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-and-batch-spike.

Samir Patel: on it. running quick query to check pod restarts: ```kubectl get pods -n inference | grep search-pool && kubectl describe pod gpu-inference-2-6f4b```

Samir Patel: I see restarts 3x in last 5m, image pull fine. check dmesg for OOM?

Luca Marino: If OOM, we should fail over to the smaller-model variant (search-compact) before paging SRE lead. Fallback policy is in the routing playbook.

Maria Chen: agreed — fallback to search-compact is our first graceful degradation. That keeps latency but reduces quality slightly. If that still fails, escalate to eng-sre.

Priya Rao: I can flip routing weight to compact now, unless anyone objects. That will drop perf for some queries but avoids customer-visible errors.

Chad Nguyen: go ahead Priya. Also add a temporary cache-bypass: set header `X-Prefer-Compact: true` for critical customer buckets while we stabilize.

Priya Rao: flipping weight 75% -> 100% to search-compact for EU: ```curl -X POST https://config.redwood/api/route -d '{"route":"/search","variant":"search-compact","region":"eu","weight":100}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CFG_TOKEN'```

Ops Bot: Deployment change recorded by Priya Rao at 21:07 UTC. :white_check_mark:

Maria Chen: monitoring for error rate and latency. If error rate remains >20% for 10m, page SRE lead (Pager: eng-sre-lead). If latency > 400ms 95p for critical customers, page product-ops. Escalation matrix: - P0: page eng-sre lead + oncall manager; - P1: page primary SRE only; - P2: slack thread/watch.

Samir Patel: after the switch error rate dropped to 6% and latency stable at 210ms 95p. good so far.

Priya Rao: leaving a note for handoff: primary until 02:00 UTC (Maria), secondary Samir for first hour, then Priya 22:00-02:00 UTC. If both unavailable escalate to Luca (oncall-rotation-lead).

Maria Chen: runbook pointers in case this recurs: - Routing fallback: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/routing-fallback - KV cache eviction check: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-and-batch-spike - OOM debugging checklist: `dmesg | grep -i oom`, `journalctl -u kubelet`, `kubectl describe pod <pod>`

Priya Rao: small note for whoever takes over: if you see repeated OOMs on gpu nodes, add temporary node taint `NoSchedule` for model-heavy nodes and spin up `search-fallback` pool on smaller instances. Example command: ```kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-3 dedicated=heavy:NoSchedule```

Chad Nguyen: customer-impact assessment: only a small set of customers running long-context retrieval were affected (approx 3 customers, not enterprise tier). I opened a support ticket and pinged CS to mitigate.

Maria Chen: decision log: 21:07 switched traffic to search-compact (mitigation). 21:12 monitoring green. No P0 declared.

Incident Bot: Incident INC-4321 closed (mitigated) by Priya Rao. Duration: 00:12:14.

Samir Patel: quick lessons: consider lowering max batch size on the heavy model during traffic surges. I'll add a proposal to Optimize for next sprint.

Maria Chen: thanks team. handoff to Priya at 22:00 UTC — leave a one-line summary in #eng-oncall when you pick up. If you need to page, follow the escalation rules above and ping me if immediate help is needed. :thumbsup:

Priya Rao: acknowledged. I'll be primary at 22:00 UTC and will post a warm-handoff message then with state + invite to the bridge if any anomalies.

Luca Marino: FYI I scheduled a quick postmortem sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC to go over batching knobs and node sizing. Invite sent to eng-sre and runtime teams.

Maria Chen: closing thread — leaving all runbook links + decision log in the incident doc. Good job everyone.

Chad Nguyen: :rocket:
